Architecture.description:
The architectures a kernel requirement may accept.

The spellings are mkosi's own `Architecture=` values, so the same word
travels from the product input manifest into the image configuration
without translation. An architecture outside this list does not decode.

ArtifactExpectation.description:
The digest and signature a conforming artifact is expected to carry.

The digest is mandatory inside this object, so a payload cannot promise a
signature over nothing; a requirement that expects neither omits the object
entirely. Both are field encodings: this crate produces and verifies
neither.

digest.description: The sha256 the produced artifact must hash to.

signature.description: The signature over that digest, when one is expected.

probe.description: How the claim is checked on a running system.

required-by.description:
The requirement this row comes from.

Schema-generic (D103): any identifier [`RequirementId`] admits, such as
a producer's `FLAVOR-BASE`. A payload Aegis issues names a recorded
requirement, which [`RequirementId::is_aegis_requirement`] tells apart.

state.description: The state that symbol must be in.

symbol.description: The Kconfig symbol the requirement is about.

KernelAbi.description: The kernel version and module ABI the requirement is bounded by.

minimum-release.description: The oldest release the requirement admits. A hard floor.

module-abi.description:
The exact module ABI a conforming artifact reports, when one is fixed.

`None` while the artifact does not exist yet: a kernel that has not
been built has no ABI to demand.

target-release.description:
The release the requirement aims at, when one is named.

Recorded, never checked against a profile. The M01 drift register's
`target kernel floor` row states that the target version named by the
sources is not a released version, so a check against it would refuse
every kernel that exists.

KernelRequirementVersion.description: The contract versions of the kernel requirement this build admits.

ProbeSource.description:
How a feature claim is checked on a running system.

Each variant names one interface, and [`Self::path`] is the exact path the
probe reads. A row therefore carries its own falsification recipe: a
reviewer runs [`FeatureRequirement::probe_command`] and compares.

oneOf.description: The kernel BTF blob CO-RE eBPF programs compile against.
The powercap tree the RAPL energy counters appear under.
The IOMMU group tree VFIO passthrough needs.

RequiredState.description: The state a requirement row demands of its symbol.

oneOf.description: The symbol must be compiled in; a module does not satisfy it.
The symbol must be a loadable module; built-in does not satisfy it.
The symbol must be available either way.
The symbol must not be enabled at all.

architectures.description:
The architectures a conforming kernel must be built for: all of them.

All-of and fail-closed (D104). A kernel conforms only when it is built
for every listed architecture and each of those builds provides every
feature; no listed architecture is optional. A repeated architecture is
one promise, evaluated once.

artifact.description: What a conforming artifact must hash and be signed to, when known.

correlation-id.description: The identifier threading this requirement and its result together.

features.description: The features a conforming kernel must provide, on every architecture.

schema.description: The contract version this payload claims.
